## 👍 Quick “Yes‑you‑can‑do‑it” plan (Amber)

I’ll give you a one‑screen plan and then walk you through each tiny step.  
Everything is at risk level **Amber** (personal data + paid API – Stripe + Supabase).  
All keys will stay secret, each user gets only their own credit, and we’ll add a tiny
dashboard to see the credit.

> **What we’re building:** A “referral” button that lets a new user use a code to get £10
> credit, and the referrer gets a record that they sent a friend.  
> **Who uses it:** Anyone who signs up.  
> **Day‑one features:**  
> 1. A “Get referral code” button on the signup page.  
> 2. Guest can paste code on checkout to get £10.  
> 3. Referrer sees a small line that says “You sent X friends”.  
> **Information stored:**  
> - `referrals` table: `id`, `referrer_id`, `invitee_id`, `credit_awarded` (bool), `created_at`.  
> - User’s credit (a custom `credit` column in the `profiles` table, stored as integer cents).  
> **Logins:** Supabase Auth + Magic link.  
> **Money:** Stripe checkout for paid plans, but the £10 credit is free.  
> **Built with:** Next.js 13 + supabase‑js, stripe‑checkout, server‑less functions.  
> **Safety notes:**  
> - All keys live in `.env` (Never in the browser).  
> - DB row‑level security keeps tables private.  
> - We add a RLS policy that only allows a user to see their own referrals.  
> - The £10 credit is *deducted* when they first spend credit in a purchase; it’s a one‑time
>   free credit.  
> **Next step:** *Approve the plan* (answer “yes” or tweak the wording). Once you say yes,
> we’ll create the DB table, add a server‑less API route, update the signup page, and
> add a small dashboard widget.

> **Does this look right?**  
> Reply `yes` or edit something (e.g., “I don’t want a dashboard widget”) and we’ll jump in.
